title: Intrinsic recovery of the grading projectors
as_he_states: Recover the degree projectors from the polarized graded ring and prove that a compatible graded overring containing the Lefschetz data contains them.
plausible_today: For the finite Lefschetz graded-ring framework, recover the complete orthogonal family intrinsically; retain the grading and support conditions when changing rings.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Theorem3.15, p.382, proves intrinsic projectors in the Lefschetz-ring setting. The manuscript extremal-degree induction agrees after the displayed terminal index is corrected mathematically, without changing its ink.
why_open: The pages give an induction rather than a missing general conjecture; the present obstacle is the confirmed erroneous terminal index.
worth: Yes, as a short companion proof that makes the precise ring hypotheses and the slip transparent.

title: Algebraicity of normalized lowering from inverse Lefschetz maps
as_he_states: Supply the proof that the indicated algebra contains the normalized Λ; later pages propose an induction using ξ and its inverse maps.
plausible_today: In a graded algebra stable under transposition and containing the Lefschetz operator and inverse hard-Lefschetz maps, construct every degree/primitive projector and normalized Λ by finite algebraic expressions.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 §§2.9–2.10 and3.15 give the established equivalences; the explicit induction on the leaves is independently type-checked in computations.md §§1–2. This is a conditional algebra lemma, not a proof of the standard conjecture for arbitrary varieties.
why_open: The first occurrence explicitly leaves a proof to provide; the later induction supplies its mechanism but has exponent slips.
worth: Yes, because a complete typed induction is short and reusable throughout the dossier.

title: Uniqueness from L without a specified grading
as_he_states: The initial ungraded universal formulation asks whether the projectors and inverse data are forced by L; a circled negative answer is followed by added grading/projector compatibility.
plausible_today: Uniqueness holds only with the compatible graded Lefschetz structure specified; as an ungraded assertion it fails by conjugation with a unit commuting with L.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 uses the graded framework. C03 gives g=1+tL and the conjugate projectors explicitly, retaining L while changing the grading.
why_open: Withdrawn in the manuscript itself, which adds the missing data.
worth: Only as a concise counterexample and explanation of the correction, not as an open theorem.

title: A top-power test for an alternative polarization
as_he_states: A tentative criterion would make a degree-two element Lefschetz when its top power is nonzero; the later example rejects it.
plausible_today: The full collection of determinants of L^(n−i):H^i→H^(2n−i) must be nonzero. Nonzero top power alone suffices only in special graded algebras.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Proposition2.10 concerns independence of an already-Lefschetz polarization, not this criterion. C04 reconstructs the stated Poincaré algebra with dimensions1,2,2,1 and an element with nonzero cube but singular middle map.
why_open: The author supplies a counterexample on the later leaf.
worth: Only to document the precise failure and distinguish the Lefschetz open set from the top-power open set.

title: Realizing an arbitrary alternating form in the four-form construction
as_he_states: After choosing a nondegenerate four-form pairing on Λ²V and α=id, a suitable ξ should give any desired nondegenerate alternating form up to a scalar.
plausible_today: The linear isomorphism Λ²V→(Λ²V)^∨ realizes any alternating covector, but imposing simultaneously a normalized square for ξ and the intended inverse-bivector convention is an additional condition. Restrict to the explicit family where all conditions are checked.
state_of_art: Searches for this exact algebraic construction in standard-conjecture/Hodge-algebra sources did not locate a published arbitrary-form theorem. The linear realization is proved directly; C08–C10 verify associativity and a rational family without treating it as proof of the unrestricted assertion.
why_open: The pages supply the construction but not the compatibility argument for all normalizations. No historical explanation was found.
worth: Yes, once the remaining notation is checked on the scan; the normalization question is elementary and sharply bounded.

title: Infinite and unbounded cyclic orbits in the Hodge-algebra example
as_he_states: The endomorphism induced by the tensor square of the inverse alternating form should have infinite orbits of ξ and the inverse bivector, already in dimension4 or6, with spans of unbounded dimension as V grows.
plausible_today: Under the explicit contraction convention in computations.md, there are rational examples in dimension6 with infinite orbit and a family in dimensions4m whose cyclic span has dimension at least m. The literal minimal dimension remains a scan/normalization question.
state_of_art: Searches of the standard-conjecture and algebraic Hodge-form literature found no exact development of this proposed countermodel. C09 gives the complete rational matrix and determinant; C10 gives a nonvanishing-minor argument for arbitrarily large spans. These are present-run constructions, not attributed to a later author.
why_open: The leaf explicitly hesitates between dimensions4 and6 and abbreviates the tensor-contraction convention.
worth: Yes, after checking the operator notation on the ink; a short follow-up could determine the sharp minimum.

title: Descent and ascent through a hyperplane section
as_he_states: An initially stronger equivalence for a variety and a smooth hyperplane section is cancelled; the retained claim transfers the Lefschetz algebraicity condition from X to Y.
plausible_today: For a smooth ample hyperplane inclusion, weak/hard Lefschetz and the typed formula ΛY=i*ΛX²i* (last i* denoting Gysin in the original distinction) prove the one-way transfer. Use i^*ΛX²i_* in modern notation.

title: The first unresolved standard-conjecture cases
as_he_states: After curves, surfaces and abelian varieties, the main difficulties already arise for one-cycles on threefolds, partly in characteristic0.
plausible_today: The Lefschetz standard conjecture remains a general problem for smooth projective varieties; known classes must be stated individually and no all-threefold claim follows from the classical cases.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1969 pp.196–197 and Kleiman1968 give the classical cases and implications. Tankeev2011 proves the standard conjecture for the specified complex projective threefolds of Kodaira dimension less than3; the opened primary abstract verifies that scope, not a proof for all threefolds.

worth: A focused survey is useful; an unrestricted proof is beyond one short research run.

title: Replacing the failed smooth-hypersurface reduction by singular hypersurfaces
as_he_states: The route through birational smooth models, specialization and smooth hypersurfaces fails because it forces simple connectivity; reformulate the standard conjectures for singular varieties if hypersurfaces are still to be used.
plausible_today: Formulate a particular singular cohomology/motive framework and specify which correspondence operators, dualities and specializations preserve the desired conjecture. No universal smooth reduction survives the given obstruction.
state_of_art: The exact sentence and the cancelled route were checked. Grothendieck1969 and Kleiman1968 formulate the smooth projective standard conjectures; searches did not identify a theorem realizing this precise singular-hypersurface reduction. Modern singular theories alone do not establish the proposed reduction.

title: Polarization independence of the algebraic Lefschetz condition
as_he_states: The first letter doubts polarization independence in characteristicp; the later letter gives a proposition using algebraic isomorphisms with dual degrees.
plausible_today: For a fixed Weil cohomology satisfying the stated Lefschetz setup, algebraicity of the inverse Lefschetz operators is independent of the choice of an ample polarization, by the algebraicity of inverses of algebraic cohomological isomorphisms.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Propositions2.9–2.11 establish this conditional equivalence and independence. The rational characteristic-polynomial/Cayley–Hamilton argument on the later leaf is checked separately; this does not settle independence of all cohomology theories.
why_open: The later manuscript proposition resolves the earlier doubt under its precise hypotheses.
worth: Yes for a short linked commentary; it is a settled internal correction.

title: Independence of the chosen cohomology theory in characteristicp
as_he_states: Unlike characteristic0, the author has no proof that the lettered standard-conjecture conditions are independent of ℓ or the cohomology theory, and asks that this dependence be acknowledged.
plausible_today: Separate polarization independence from comparison of cycle classes across cohomologies. Finite-field Frobenius and Künneth results are established; the broad comparison requires additional conjectures and does not follow from equal Betti numbers.
state_of_art: KatzMessing1974 Theorem1 and Corollary1, pp.74–75, compare Frobenius polynomials for reasonable theories; Theorem2, pp.76–77, gives common algebraic Künneth projectors in its Weil/crystalline setting. These narrower exact results do not prove every lettered standard conjecture independent of the theory.
why_open: The author explicitly attributes his earlier haste to transferring characteristic0 intuition.
worth: Yes as a carefully delimited comparison table; a general independence theorem remains a major problem.

title: A semisimple motive category with cohomological realizations
as_he_states: Construct the semisimple category of motives suggested by the conditional semisimplicity of the algebra of cohomological correspondences, and split cohomological injections algebraically.
plausible_today: Numerical motives with rational coefficients form a semisimple abelian category. To factor a chosen cohomological realization through numerical equivalence requires numerical=homological equivalence; it is not supplied by numerical semisimplicity alone.
state_of_art: Kleiman1968 Theorems3.12–3.14 give the conditional cohomological statements. Jannsen1992 Theorem1, p.448, proves semisimplicity for numerical motives without the standard conjectures; Corollary1 clarifies the equivalence-relation condition.
why_open: The manuscript programme predates the distinction made decisive by the later numerical-category theorem; no source inspected claims the realization gap is automatically removed.
worth: Yes: this is a high-value clarification of an often conflated settled theorem and remaining conjecture.

title: Deduction of the Weil conjectures and the missing positivity input
as_he_states: Deduce the Weil conjectures from the lettered Lefschetz/algebraicity conditions in an extra paragraph.
plausible_today: The classical route needs Hodge-type positivity as well as algebraic Lefschetz correspondences; the abbreviated two-letter statement must be read with the index conjecture in the surrounding letters. The Weil conjectures themselves are now established independently of a proof of all standard conjectures.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1969 p.197 explicitly includes the Hodge standard conjecture in the implication. KatzMessing1974 then uses Deligne’s theorem for the finite-field comparison consequences. The sources do not make general positive-characteristic algebraic positivity a theorem.
why_open: The text abbreviates assumptions across editorial letters rather than giving a complete isolated theorem.
worth: Yes as a hypothesis audit; it should not be framed as an unresolved Weil-conjecture proof.
problem_origin: author requested exposition; present-run hypothesis audit

title: The way-out RHom coherence exercise
as_he_states: Prove the corollary on coherence of RHom by way-out functors under the explicit uniform vanishing of Ext from coherent sheaves.
plausible_today: On a noetherian scheme, use the stated uniform Ext bound and coherent input cohomology to reduce each output degree to finitely many truncations. The result is coherence, with boundedness only when separately assumed.
state_of_art: Stacks0D0C Lemma36.11.5 gives the D−coherent/D+coherent case; Stacks0G4H Lemma47.15.2 gives finite-injective-dimension coherence. C12 explains why dropping the uniform control can produce an infinite product in a single degree.
why_open: The author expressly leaves a good exercise, not an unsolved conjecture.
worth: Yes, because the finite-window proof and the exact meaning of coherent are short and useful.

The exact broad one-line manuscript formulation needs the surrounding draft hypotheses, not a remembered blanket theorem.

as_he_states: Define the Dedekind different through the trace and prove equality with the Kähler different for discrete valuation rings.

title: The transformed-line-bundle character and Chern coefficients
as_he_states: Compute the transformed line bundle formally as χ times an exponential/fractional line and infer Chern classes and divisibility.
plausible_today: In the ample algebraically closed field case, φL*Φ(L)≅H0(L)⊗L^−1 and chΦ(L)=r exp(−D′/r). The corrected kth Chern coefficient is (−1)^k(r−1)…(r−k+1)/(k!r^(k−1)); no fractional line bundle is asserted.

title: The particular line-bundle formulas modulo torsion
as_he_states: Are the preceding formulas true modulo torsion?
plausible_today: For the specified transformed ample bundle over a field, rational identities yield integral equalities modulo torsion after denominators are cleared. The relative K/Gr interpretation needs specification; the question does not assert an integral Fourier operator on every Chow class.

EngelFortmanSchreieder2025/2026 Theorem1.1 refutes that stronger extrapolation for very general complex PPAVs of dimension≥4. Kahn2026 Theorem1.2/Corollary1.3 gives an étale-Chow replacement after inverting the characteristic and quotienting a subgroup killed by2. Neither comparison is misreported as a full answer to the narrower literal question.

title: Todd factors in relative Riemann–Roch
as_he_states: Translate the Fourier formulas into cohomological/Riemann–Roch formulas and simplify the Todd factors.

It is not an arbitrary-base blanket simplification.

worth: Yes, as a short two-setting comparison that prevents loss of the base correction.

title: Orthogonality of the two Frobenius kernels
as_he_states: Under Cartier duality of A[p] and B[p], the Frobenius kernels FA and FB should be orthogonal.
plausible_today: For dual abelian varieties over a perfect field of characteristicp, transpose of Frobenius is Verschiebung; ker(FB) is the annihilator of ker(FA) with the appropriate twists and the indicated exact sequences.
state_of_art: Oda1969 Corollary5.11 gives the compatible Hodge/Dieudonné description; the manuscript F–V sequences and ranks p^g versus p^(2g) are checked directly. The Frobenius twists are essential.

title: Recovering the de Rham extension from A[p]
as_he_states: Can the restricted-Lie extension, hence the indicated de Rham extension, be deduced from the group scheme pA?
plausible_today: For an abelian variety over a perfect field of characteristicp, the full Dieudonné module of A[p] canonically identifies with H1dR(A), including the Hodge sequence and F,V. Restricted Lie data alone are a weaker invariant.
state_of_art: Oda1969 Corollary5.11, p.131, proves exactly the abelian H1 statement, following the1967 thesis and Grothendieck’s1966 p.102 suggestion. Corollary5.12, p.132, gives only a specified injection for general smooth proper X. SGA3VIIb Theorem4.4/Corollary4.4.1 treats height-one groups and p-Lie algebras, not all of A[p].

title: The generic closed flattening locus of Proposition A
as_he_states: For nonempty Y, f:X→Y of finite presentation and an F of finite presentation, find a nonempty open U and a closed Z⊂U universally characterizing flatness of the pulled-back F.
plausible_today: Retain arbitrary nonempty Y. Reduce by noetherian approximation; on the reduced generic locus apply generic freeness, then use the ideal controlling flatness across the nilpotent thickening.
state_of_art: Stacks051R Lemma10.118.1 gives generic freeness;0525 Lemma15.17.2 and05MZ Lemma38.24.1 give exact local flattening-ideal results. Computations.md §12 supplies the nilpotent-basis proof and explains the noetherian approximation. Properness is not silently inserted.
why_open: The page sketches the reduction and cites a flattening-ideal lemma without proving it.
worth: Yes as a compact proof of the exact statement, with arbitrary-base scope preserved.

title: Cancelled generic-freeness and ideal-separation variants
as_he_states: Try to pass from flatness at p to freeness after localization and to use ideal separation; parts are cancelled or weakened.
plausible_today: Separate generic freeness of finite modules over finite-type algebras from arbitrary localization/flatness statements. Retain only the finite-presentation/noetherian hypotheses of the established lemma.
state_of_art: Stacks051R gives the exact generic-freeness theorem; the cancelled layers were read individually. No claim that every arbitrary flat module becomes finite free on a neighbourhood is adopted.
why_open: The author changes and cancels the formulations on the page; their full intended scope is not recovered from the fragment.
worth: Only as a correction map supporting Proposition A, not as a new broad flatness conjecture.

title: Faithfulness of graded completion on the TF subcategory
as_he_states: After cancelling the main argument, retain that completion on graded TF modules is exact and faithful.
plausible_today: For a noetherian nonnegative graded ring with adic degree filtration, completion is flat; on finitely generated graded modules it is the product of graded pieces and is faithful. For the larger undefined TF class, the exact definition and the decomposition into a finite tail plus a bounded-above part are needed.
state_of_art: Stacks00MB Lemma10.97.2 proves noetherian completion flatness/exactness on finite modules;00MC Lemma10.97.3 gives faithful flatness only when the ideal lies in the Jacobson radical. The graded finite-module argument is proved separately, without asserting faithful flatness on all ungraded modules.
why_open: TF is not defined in the supplied page, and the body of the argument is cancelled.
worth: Yes for context/ink recovery; the finite graded case itself is routine.
problem_origin: author retained assertion with undefined condition

title: Albanese equivalence and the kernel attached to a family
as_he_states: Define the family quotient Pξ by the common kernel and identify the relation on cycles as a form of Albanese equivalence.
plausible_today: Use universal regular homomorphisms of algebraically trivial cycles when representable. The manuscript’s kernel/intersection construction must be proved to have that universal property before identifying the quotient with a modern algebraic representative.
state_of_art: Kahn2021 Theorem1, pp.843–848, repairs Murre’s codimension2 proof; ACMV2023 Theorem6.1 gives algebraic representatives for codimensions1,2 and dimX under its smooth proper hypotheses. They do not automatically prove this particular all-codimension family quotient universal.
why_open: The letter says the relation is not yet identified and little has been proved; no later source inspected identifies the literal construction in every degree.
worth: Yes, starting in codimension2 where a modern universal object exists.

title: The half-Betti-number bound
as_he_states: The proposed Pξ or Ji should have dimension at most half b_(2i−1).
plausible_today: For an algebraic representative whose rational Tate module injects into H^(2i−1), the dimension bound follows. Its application to an undefined all-codimension quotient requires a comparison theorem.
state_of_art: ACMV2023 Proposition8.2 gives an integral injection away from the characteristic and miniversal-cycle degree for i=1,2,dimX; rationally this yields the dimension bound in those cases. Theorem9.5 identifies the complex representatives with algebraic intermediate Jacobians in those degrees.
why_open: The manuscript ties the bound to an unproved cohomological realization of the proposed quotient.
worth: Yes, by proving the bound in the represented cases and stating the missing map elsewhere.

title: All-codimension intermediate algebraic Jacobians and complementary duality
as_he_states: Construct Ji in every codimension with J1=Pic0, Jn=Alb0, and Ji dual to J^(n+1−i).
plausible_today: Universal regular homomorphisms give the established algebraic representatives in codimensions1,2 and n; complex algebraic intermediate Jacobians are related but their Abel–Jacobi maps need not be universally regular in higher codimension. Complementary duality requires its own construction and hypotheses.
state_of_art: Kahn2021 proves codimension2 and states a specific conjectural higher-codimension obstruction; ACMV2023 Theorems6.1 and9.5 give precise positive cases. OttemSuzuki2020 Corollary4.2 exhibits a codimension3 Abel–Jacobi map that is not universal although a universal object exists up to nontrivial isogeny.
why_open: The author expressly calls these conjectures and has not identified the equivalence relation. No source inspected supplies the unrestricted programme.
worth: High interest, but first compare the literal quotient with the codimension2 representative; all codimensions exceed a short run.

title: Positivity of the cycle-family correspondence
as_he_states: After quotienting by the kernel of the symmetric divisor correspondence, prove positivity; primitive decomposition must be taken into account.
plausible_today: Distinguish a symmetric homomorphism/isogeny from an ample polarization. Use the sign (−1)^(i−1), the primitive decomposition and explicit realization hypotheses; in positive characteristic require an appropriate theorem or standard conjecture.
state_of_art: ACMV2025 Theorem12.6, pp.66–67, constructs symmetric maps/isogenies under Bloch/Tate hypotheses; Theorem12.12, p.68, gives a distinguished autoduality for universally CH0-trivial threefolds. Its negative is the principal Hodge polarization over C; Chapter13 treats positive-characteristic polarization with lifting hypotheses. Grothendieck1969 and Kleiman1968 state the broader primitive positivity conjecture.
why_open: The author explicitly asks for a proof and warns that primitives were initially ignored.
worth: High interest; a few-hour run can settle conventions and known threefold cases, not general positive-characteristic positivity.

title: Intersection formulas for the proposed Néron–Tate pairing
as_he_states: Relate the pairing of fibrewise algebraically trivial cycles in a pencil to (−1)^m times the intersection of their total-space extensions, and formulate a general/local version.
plausible_today: Require proper regular models and admissible vertical corrections/orthogonality so the intersection is independent of the chosen extensions. Fix the codimensions and sign before comparison with the abelian height.
state_of_art: Kunnemann2001 §1 and Theorem1.6/Corollary1.7 give the regular-model height pairing and the abelian-variety case over number fields. KahnHeight2024 Definition2.10 and Theorem4.14 construct refined heights for admissible cycle groups over function fields; Theorem5.10 identifies the elliptic-curve convention with the opposite refined height. These are not a proof of the raw uncorrected intersection formula in every pencil.
why_open: The leaf leaves vertical corrections, the middle-dimensional sign and the general fibration statement unfinished.
worth: Yes, beginning with the elliptic-surface case where all normalizations can be checked explicitly.
problem_origin: author requested generalization and sign verification

title: Hyperplane and pencil restriction for the proposed Pi
as_he_states: Expect Lefschetz-type isomorphism, fixed-part and surjectivity statements for Pi, with a stronger clause cancelled.
plausible_today: First define Pi as an algebraic representative in a degree where it exists, then specify the map induced by restriction or Gysin. The fixed part and a rational realization statement do not automatically imply the claimed integral isomorphism.
state_of_art: ACMV2023 Theorem9.5 gives the represented complex cases and Proposition8.2 the Tate realization with its excluded primes. Grothendieck1969/Kleiman1968 give cohomological Lefschetz conditions; no exact all-Pi pencil theorem matching the unfinished leaf was identified.
why_open: The text cancels a stronger formulation and does not establish the objects or integral comparison needed for the remainder.
worth: Yes after the codimension2 identification; do not begin by treating every displayed map as already defined.
problem_origin: author open assertions and cancelled stronger formulation

title: Numerical equivalence versus τ-equivalence
as_he_states: State numerical equivalence=τ-equivalence, with a marginal attribution to Matsusaka.
plausible_today: For divisors the familiar numerical/algebraic-modulo-torsion comparison is appropriate. In all codimensions, if τ means that a nonzero integer multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero, the equality is false.
state_of_art: Clemens1983 Theorem0.2/Corollary0.3, pp.19–20, gives nontorsion Griffiths classes on a generic quintic threefold; these are homologically and hence numerically trivial but not algebraically trivial modulo torsion. The exact definition of τ on the leaf remains a reading/context issue.
why_open: The likely divisor theorem is extended in an abbreviated all-cycle setting without its necessary restriction; the supplied page does not define τ.
worth: Yes to identify the intended scope and prevent a false all-codimension attribution.
problem_origin: present-run scope verification of an asserted theorem

title: Integral Tate realization: subquotient or submodule
as_he_states: Tℓ(Ji) should be a subquotient of H^(2i−1)(X,Zℓ(i)), and eventually even a submodule.
plausible_today: For the represented degrees1,2,n use a miniversal cycle and exclude primes dividing its degree for the direct integral injection; distinguish rational, prime-to-degree and all-prime statements.
state_of_art: ACMV2023 Proposition8.2, p.31, gives the injection away from the characteristic and miniversal degree. ACMV2025 Proposition10.3, pp.50–51, gives stronger Tate-module isomorphisms under characteristic0 or the stated cohomological diagonal-decomposition hypotheses; Definition10.5 makes the remaining standard assumption explicit.
why_open: The author explicitly distinguishes the weak and stronger integral formulations; existence of Ji and torsion control are both missing in general.
worth: High interest as a precise integral comparison problem, first in codimension2 at the excluded primes.

title: The tangent-space Hodge realization
as_he_states: Conjecturally t_(Ji) lies in H^i(X,Ω_X^(i−1)), and in characteristic0 Hodge cohomology should replace Weil cohomology.
plausible_today: For complex algebraic intermediate Jacobians, the tangent realization is obtained from the relevant Hodge quotient and its algebraic subtorus. An inclusion into the displayed single Hodge group requires fixing duality/index conventions; it is not automatically an all-characteristic tangent theorem.
state_of_art: ACMV2023 Theorem9.5 identifies algebraic representatives with algebraic intermediate Jacobians in degrees1,2,n over subfields of C. Coleman1998 verifies the i=1 abelian Hodge-extension comparison. No exact theorem giving the manuscript inclusion for every i and arbitrary characteristic was located.
why_open: The margin is explicitly conjectural and the source does not fix the variance of the tangent realization.
worth: Yes as a Hodge-index check in the represented complex cases, with generalization kept separate.
